If you haven't been following recent developments at Voat, the following /v/voatdev announcements will help get you up to speed on what Putt's focus has been since the Port was mostly completed:

  • Beta Feature: Subverse Rules
  • Alpha Preview: Voat Votes
  • Beta Feature: External Stickies
  • Subverse Rules Feature (Beta 2)

Basically, progress has been made towards altering the structures of subverses themselves by making rules into something that can be more easily interacted with (and therefore used more directly in code), and the ability to apply stickies has changed -- not only can three stickies be applied per subverse, but subverses can sticky threads from other subverses within their own subverses. Note: These changes are only in place on the preview site and have not yet been implemented on live Voat.

Beyond these changes, a great deal of time has been put forth on the vote feature (see the second thread in the bullet list above). As I've already discussed, this feature, being a large and seemingly radical change, has been met with some resistance. As I have also discussed, all paths Putt treads down, especially at the current time, will be met with considerable resistance. Perhaps by elaborating on some of the details of these votes here I can relieve some of those opposed to the feature.

First off, there are categories for votes in subverses. This feature may differ somewhat between its present testing form on the preview and final implementation, but at present there is a consideration for how votes will work depending on the subverse. The Private category only allows polls (votes that have no automatic outcome). This may apply to only actual private subverses, or perhaps also small subverses -- it is unclear. The Public category allows referenda (votes with outcomes) as well as polls, and can have multiple outcomes per option, and multiple restrictions. The System category (to ultimately apply to @system subverses) allows referenda as well but limits options to one outcome and limits the restrictions on voting to 1.

NOTE: votes as they exist on the preview at present are for testing; the majority of votes actually created on live Voat when this feature goes live will be done through templates of various forms.

Votes will mostly be started through templates. These, I gather, will be votes will all (or most) fields already filled in to begin a vote for a specific outcome. As Putt says in the thread I just linked to, the only template currently live on the preview site is the subverse transfer template. This should excite a number of users; through the votes feature, votes will be automatically generated whenever users apply for a subverse request (essentially), and this will give the community a chance to vote on the outcome. For one, the user applying for the transfer will have to meet all of the rules already in place for subverse transfers. If all conditions are met, the vote will go live and the community will be able to vote on the proposed new owner. There will be restrictions on who can vote depending on a number of things.

I've said a lot about voting restrictions an requirements without elaborating much. Basically, certain vote templates for certain actions will have varying restrictions as to who can actually vote on certain outcomes. So mod bans will require certain things in order for votes to actually "count" towards an outcome; subverse transfers will require other restrictions; rule additions other restrictions still, etc. This means that almost no outcome vote will be straight democracy -- most outcomes will ensure that only those who have "skin in the game" can control the outcome. This eliminates the state of absolute democracy for most vote types.

See this comment I've already linked to: "It is the combination of outcomes, restrictions, and thresholds that will limit what can pass and what can't. ". So it will be virtually impossible to game any vote once the templates are set up properly. This should limit most concerns about abuse, leaving only those who are opposed to democracy in any form on principle. To this minority of complainants, I say:

For one, as far as I can tell /v/whatever will be untouched by any vote templates. Rule 99 prevents people from subverse transferring it to themselves; Rules of course won't be added; perhaps there will be vote templates for Janitors in /v/whatever, but I don't see anything beyond that.

Furthermore, something has to be done in order to make Voat functional again. Subverse transfers are just one example of what needs attention, and Putt does not have the time to handle all of Voat by himself. If this feature can be implemented correctly (and as Putt has said, it will need vetting and careful testing), it should be able to allow Voat to run smoothly without compromising communities or giving groups any control. Those who actually contribute to communities will have the most say on how those communities proceed through time. As a long term solution this one seems to have great promise.

DISCLAIMER: I've tried to rely on direct links but I still may have misrepresented or poorly worded some of these ideas. The best way to come to understand the votes feature is to do reading on it yourself.
